message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | Key Rights | Practical Tips | |------|------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and a receipt of the deposit.
• Request a written itemized list of deductions if you disagree. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, etc.).
• Must repair major defects within a reasonable time after notice. | • Document problems with photos and written notices.
• If repairs are not made, you may withhold rent or pursue a repair‑and‑deduct claim. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed only if stated in the lease. | • Pay by check, money order, or electronic transfer to avoid disputes. | | **Lease Termination** | • **Month‑to‑month** tenants can terminate with **30 days’ written notice**.
• Landlords must give **30 days’ notice** to terminate a month‑to‑month lease. | • Keep a copy of the notice and send it via certified mail or email with read receipt. | | **Eviction** | • Landlord must provide a **written notice** (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease violation).
• Eviction must go through the court; landlords cannot forcibly remove you. | • Respond promptly to notices; negotiate or seek mediation if possible. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord may enter only for **reasonable reasons** (repairs, inspections, emergencies) and must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours). | • Keep a log of all entries; if you suspect unlawful entry, document it. | | **Discrimination** | • Protected under the **Fair Housing Act**: no discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income. | • Report violations to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Maintenance of Records** | • Landlord must keep records of rent payments and maintenance requests. | • Keep copies of all correspondence and receipts. | | **Repair‑and‑Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major defect, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but you must follow the proper procedure (notice, receipts, etc.). | • Use reputable contractors and keep receipts. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has **no statewide rent control**; rent increases are governed by the lease terms. | • Review lease clauses on rent increases; negotiate if needed. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord may require you to pay utilities unless otherwise specified. | • Verify which utilities are your responsibility in the lease. | | **Subletting** | • You may sublet only with landlord’s written consent, unless the lease allows it. | • Get written permission and keep a copy. | | **Insurance** | • Landlord is not required to provide renter’s insurance, but you are encouraged to obtain it. | • Consider liability and personal property coverage. | | **Legal Remedies** | • If your rights are violated, you can file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office, HUD, or the local housing agency. | • Small claims court can be used for disputes under $10,000. | #### Quick Checklist for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Thoroughly** – Understand rent amount, due date, security deposit limits, and notice periods. 2. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, written notices, and receipts. 3. **Know the Notice Requirements** – 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month termination, 3‑day notice for nonpayment, 30‑day notice for lease violations. 4. **Keep Copies of All Correspondence** – Emails, letters, and notices. 5. **Report Discrimination** – Contact HUD or the Texas Commission on Human Rights. 6. **Seek Legal Advice if Needed** – Tenant rights groups, legal aid clinics, or a private attorney. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and not legal advice. For specific situations, consult a licensed attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.
